raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Marlborough's Awatere Valley winds whip Chardonnay vines into focus, delivering stone fruit snap over tropical breadth. Oyster Bay skips oak entirely, locking in that coastal crispness at 12.5% ABV. This 2021 vintage earned a TEXSOM bronze for its clean lift.",
  "wine_summary": "Oyster Bay built its name on Marlborough Chardonnay that punches above everyday weight, sourcing from Wairau and Awatere subregions for balanced ripeness. The producer scales up fruit purity without losing site detail, making this a staple for New Zealand exports. Terroir here means gravelly alluvial soils and maritime chills that yield peach and lime notes with staying power.",
  "terroir_expression": "Wairau Valley's free-draining gravel and silt over clay hold heat by day for peach and melon development, while Southern Ocean winds cool nights to lock in citrus acidity. Awatere's clay-loam and gusts add herbal tension, translating to zesty green apple cut and saline minerality in the glass. These patterns explain the wine's vibrant fruit without flab.",
  "vinification_summary": "Oyster Bay ferments in stainless steel at cool temperatures to trap primary fruit aromas, then avoids malolactic fermentation—where sharp malic acid softens to creamy lactic—to maintain bright acidity. Light lees stirring adds subtle texture without oak influence, prioritizing Marlborough's site-driven flavors over added complexity.",
  "food_pairing": "Fish tacos with cabbage slaw: acidity slices through fried batter while melon notes echo creamy sauce. Nashville hot chicken: crisp structure tempers spice heat, stone fruit cools the burn. Herb-roasted whole chicken: lime zip matches lemon-thyme seasoning, body stands up to skin crisp. Seared scallops with beurre blanc: saline edge amplifies butter richness without overwhelming. Vietnamese pho ga: citrus lift cuts broth fat, herbal hints align with ginger-basil.",
  "comparable_wines": "Kim Crawford Marlborough Chardonnay — same cool-climate fruit focus and no-oak freshness at similar pricing. Villa Maria Private Bin Chardonnay — Marlborough gravel soils yield parallel peach acidity, slightly fuller body.",
  "style_profile": "Medium-bodied dry white with bright acidity and stone fruit core",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink within three years of vintage for peak fruit vibrancy. Store cool and dark; cork closure holds steady.",
  "value_assessment": "$15-18 shelf price matches entry New Zealand Chardonnay tier. Kim Crawford runs $16 with near-identical profile; Oyster Bay edges it on Awatere intensity. Buy multiples—consistent quality justifies stock-up.",
  "market_position": "Supermarket casual drinkers grab this for weeknight ease. Entry restaurant lists feature it by the glass in coastal U.S. spots. Avoid collectors; it's built for immediate quaffing.",
  "insider_take": "Chardonnay haters skip Sauvignon shadow, but this flips the script with better acid retention than most California rivals. Tradeoff is modest depth for unbeatable everyday snap—who needs oak bloat? Cellar fringe buyers, rush for 2021.",
  "aging_potential_years": 5,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 0,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 5,
  "sensory": {
    "acidity": 4,
    "tannin": 1,
    "body": 3,
    "sweetness": 1,
    "alcohol": 3,
    "color_intensity": "pale",
    "aroma_intensity": "medium",

    "complexity": "moderate",
    "quality_level": "good"
  }
}
